met_analysis:
The severe cyclonic storm “Arnab” over Coastal Andhra Pradesh & Yanam and adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal, moved slowly north-northwestwards with the speed of 8 kmph during past 6 hours, weakened into a cyclonic storm and lies centered at 1730 hrs IST of today, the 28th October, over the same region near latitude 17.0°N and longitude 81.7°E, about 60 km north of Narsapur (Andhra Pradesh), 60 km west-northwest of Yanam (Puducherry UT), 60 km west of Kakinada (Andhra Pradesh), 100 km west-southwest of Tuni (Andhra Pradesh), 110 km north-northeast of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 110 km east-northeast of Gannavaram (Andhra Pradesh). It is very likely to move north-northwestwards during next 24 hours, it is very likely to weaken into a Deep Depression by midnight of today, the 28th October, 2026 and weaken gradually thereafter.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over south Andaman Sea & neighbourhood extending upto 5.8 km above mean sea level persists. Under its influence, a low pressure area is likely to form over the same region during next 24 hours.
The cyclonic circulation over northwest Uttar Pradesh & neighbourhood now lies over Haryana & adjoining Uttar Pradesh at 1.5 km above mean sea level.
The Western Disturbance as a cyclonic circulation over Jammu and neighbourhood between 3.1 and 4.5 km above mean sea level persists. Another Western Disturbance as a trough in middle tropospheric westerlies with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level roughly along Long. 69°E to the north of Lat. 28°N persists.
